FACTS OF THE CASE 1.

Briefly stated, the facts of the case are that on 11.08.2021, at about 05:30 pm, one Shanti Devi (since deceased) was travelling alongwith her son namely Brijpal Singh, on a motorcycle bearing registration no. UP23D1098, from their village Alampurkainch to Pakbada.

It has been alleged that when they reached near Village Fatehpur Vishnoi within the jurisdiction of PS Chajlet, Distt.
Muradabad, UP, a motorcycle bearing registration no. UP21BQ3392 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle), came from the wrong side at a very high speed and hit the above-said motorcycle of the deceased.
It has been alleged that the offending vehicle was being driven in a rash and negligent manner by its driver i.e. respondent no. 1 (R1) herein, at the time of the accident.

In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is Brij Pal Singh And Ors vs Lokesh Kumar And Ors on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100640364/
4 never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

16. The only defence raised by insurance company in this case is that the petitioners have not brought the postmortem report of the deceased victim in the present case.
It has been contended that in absence of postmortem report of the deceased, it cannot be proved that the deceased died due to the injuries suffered in the accident in question only.
The fact that the postmortem report of the deceased has not been brought on record is an admitted fact.

However, the same has been duly explained by PW1 during his cross-examination wherein he has specifically stated that the intimation regarding the death of the victim was given to the police officials by the family, but, no police official responded and the deceased was thereafter cremated after waiting till 02:00 pm.
The PW1 has specifically stated during his cross-examination that they did not get the postmortem done on the body of his deceased mother since the police did not come.
The said explanation given by PW1 is reasonable and natural considering the village background of the petitioners.
On the other hand, the respondents have not led any evidence to substantiate their contention that the deceased expired due to an illness not related to the injuries suffered by her in the accident.

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his entire family.
Spousal Consortium allows compensation to surviving spouse for loss of 'company, society, co-operation, affection and aid of the other in every conjugal relation'.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court further observed in said judgment that parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of 'parental aid, protection,
affection, society, discipline, guidance and training.
Similarly, filial consortium is to be granted to each of the surviving dependent parents on the death of their child.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is tested on the touchstone of principle of preponderance of probabilities.
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is Brij Pal Singh And Ors vs Lokesh Kumar And Ors on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100640364/
4 never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs Amir Chand & Ors, 2011 (1) SCR 1906 (Civil Appeal No. 1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
11.
The fact that the postmortem report of the deceased has not been brought on record is an admitted fact.
However, the same has been duly explained by PW1 during his cross-examination wherein he has specifically stated that the intimation regarding the death of the victim was given to the police officials by the family, but, no police official responded and the deceased was thereafter cremated after waiting till 02:00 pm.
The PW1 has specifically stated during his cross-examination that they did not get the postmortem done on the body of his deceased mother since the police did not come.
The said explanation given by PW1 is reasonable and natural considering the village background of the petitioners.
On the other hand, the respondents have not led any evidence to substantiate their contention that the deceased expired due to an illness not related to the injuries suffered by her in the accident.
At the same time,
the fact that the deceased indeed suffered serious injuries on account of the accident in question is clearly revealed from the perusal of the MLC/treatment document of Deen Dayal District Hospital,
Muradabad, U.P. brought on record by the petitioers.
Therefore, in such facts and circumstances as revealed on record, the Tribunal finds no substance in the MACT No. 350/2022 Brij Pal Singh &
Ors. Vs. Lokesh Kumar & Ors. Page No. 9 of 18 Digitally signed by HARUN HARUN PRATAP PRATAP Date:
Hence, petitioners being the LRs and dependents of the deceased are entitled to compensation in this case.
At the same time, the respondent no. 03 ie.
insurance company has failed to bring on record or to prove any breach of the terms or conditions of the said insurance policy by the R1/R2 in any manner.
Hence, petitioners are not entitled to any compensation under this head on account of absence of any evidence brought on record in this regard.
LOSS OF DEPENDENCY 24.
In the present case, perusal of the Aadhar card of Shanti Devi Ex. PW1/3 reveal that date of birth of the deceased was 01.01.1956 and the same has not been disputed in any manner by the respondents.
Therefore, the deceased was thus aged about 65 years 07 months at the time of the incident resulting in his death on 11.08.2021.
25.
In absence of any documents of income or earning of the deceased filed on record, this Tribunal has assessed the income of deceased at parity with minimum wages of "unskilled worker" in U.P prevalent at the time of accident i.e. Rs. 9,078/- per month.
Therefore, the monthly income of the deceased with Nil MACT No. 350/2022 Brij Pal Singh & Ors. Vs. Lokesh Kumar & Ors.
Moreover, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of "Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr"., (2009) 6 SCC 121,
which has also been upheld by the Constitutional Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of " National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Pranay Sethi & Ors".
